2	  {
3	    "comment_id": 4439288892,
4	    "path": "apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/library/reconcile/reconcile-dialog.tsx",
5	    "line": 213,
6	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Dragging to select a file name now toggles the row (confidence medium)**\n\nThe row's `onClick` fires for any click whose target isn't the input. That includes the click Chromium sends after a drag-select when mousedown and mouseup both land inside the `<li>`. Someone who drags over `.rowNow` or `.rowAfter` to copy a long file name will untick (or re-tick) that row as a side effect. The change does show on screen (dimmed row, strikethrough, a different summary count and button label), but it's easy to miss after a copy. One fix is to skip the toggle when `window.getSelection()?.toString()` is non-empty. Another is to add `user-select: none` to `.rowSelectable`, if copying names isn't something users need.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",
7	    "replies": [
8	      {
9	        "author": "csdev19",
10	        "body": "Real, fixed in 59f6d481: the row's click handler returns early when `window.getSelection()` has text, so a drag-select over a name to copy it no longer toggles the row. The test now selects text, clicks the row and checks the box keeps its state. Kept text selectable rather than `user-select: none`, because copying long file names is useful here."
11	      }
12	    ]
13	  }
14	]

contracts.action: Row click skips the toggle when the window has a non-empty text selection
contracts.equivalent_path: The row's own onClick toggle (same file, lines 211-220) and the checkbox onChange
contracts.before_after: Before: any click outside the input toggled the row, including the click that ends a drag-select. After: a click with selected text returns early. A plain click clears the selection on mousedown, so it still toggles.
contracts.visible_effect: Dragging over a file name to copy it no longer unticks the row. A plain click on the row still toggles it, and the checkbox is unchanged.
contracts.failure_mode: window.getSelection() is optional-chained, so a null selection is safe. No async or IPC involved.

thread_replies.reply: Addressed. The row handler at reconcile-dialog.tsx:216 returns early when the window has selected text. The test covers it by mocking getSelection and checking the box keeps its state.

input.summary: The change adds a selection guard to the row click handler, and it addresses the earlier thread about drag-select toggling the row. The test covers the guard. I found no new issues.
